reasons.action: The brief explicitly requests a bricklaying performance — a bricklayer laying a course, one brick per hit — so the requested behavior governs the action. The audio reference only supplies beat and tempo, not behavior.
reasons.medium: No visual reference is supplied; the sole reference is an audio track providing rhythm, which cannot establish a rendering family, so the request governs the medium.
reasons.wardrobe: With no visual reference and no observed subject plate, there is no competing observed clothing; the request's scene is the only authority over wardrobe.
reasons.lighting: No reference image or clip supplies lighting, and the audio reference has no bearing on illumination; lighting therefore falls to the request.
reasons.framing: No visual reference anchors a composition and the audio cannot specify a shot; framing rests with the request. The 16:9 canvas and 8-second duration are output settings, not framing instructions.
reasons.palette: No visual reference provides a color or tonal treatment, and the audio reference carries no palette; the scene's palette is left to the request.
